AppliedVerdict.description: A held verdict a resume revalidated and applied: the result it became.
AppliedVerdict.title: AppliedVerdict

BatchReport.description: One task for each open dimension, served together -- or replayed by their key.
BatchReport.title: BatchReport

BatchSummary.description: A flush as identifiers: never its events, which can hold the learner's words.
BatchSummary.title: BatchSummary

BatchTask.description: One task a batch served, in the position the batch served it.
BatchTask.title: BatchTask

CloseReport.description: The one report a close returns, and the one a repeat returns again.
CloseReport.title: CloseReport

OutstandingJudgement.description:
One answer waiting on a judgement, and what it is waiting on.

Never the learner's words: this reaches the screen, which has no consent parameter to
check them against. A judge reads an answer through `pending` and `claim`. Derived from
the claim and verdict rows and the clock -- `judging.claim_states` and
`judging.held_submissions` -- never stored, so it cannot disagree with them.
OutstandingJudgement.title: OutstandingJudgement

OutstandingTask.description:
A task this run served and has not settled, as it was served.

Never from `assessment_tasks`. A pack is mutable and a run is not, so re-reading the
bank would let an edit made after the serving decide what the learner is held to have
been asked.
OutstandingTask.title: OutstandingTask

PlayReport.description: One play of a task's recording, recorded before it was heard.
PlayReport.title: PlayReport

PresentationChoice.description: One button. `value` is submitted and scored; `display` is only drawn.
PresentationChoice.title: PresentationChoice

RecordingPolicy.description:
Whether this track lets a learner record an answer for a judge, and for how long
the recording is kept.

`offered` is the gate: equipment *and* consent, never one standing in for the other.
The retention policy is reported so a page can say it, and never overridden.
RecordingPolicy.title: RecordingPolicy

RecoveredEvent.description: One staged event moved by a recovery: where it was, and the row it became.
RecoveredEvent.title: RecoveredEvent

ResumePoint.description:
Where a session should be picked up: the first block and activity not finished.

Reported rather than inferred by the caller, because inferring it needs the block
and activity statuses to be right -- which is the whole reason `session log` advances
them and the close settles them.
ResumePoint.title: ResumePoint

RunListReport.description: The runs a fresh page could resume, newest first, for one track.
RunListReport.title: RunListReport

RunScreen.description: The whole state of one run, in one read.
RunScreen.title: RunScreen

ServedAsset.description:
A recording as served: which one was meant, and which bytes were played.

Both halves, always. The content ID answers *which recording was meant*; only the
digest answers *is this the recording they heard*, which is the one question the
snapshot exists to settle.
ServedAsset.title: ServedAsset

SessionBatchReport.description: What one flush did, including doing nothing because it had already landed.
SessionBatchReport.title: SessionBatchReport

SessionListEntry.description: One session as a page deciding what to draw needs it.
SessionListEntry.title: SessionListEntry

SessionOmissionReport.description: A candidate the planner ranked highly and did not schedule.
SessionOmissionReport.title: SessionOmissionReport

SessionScreen.description: Everything a page needs to draw one session, read on one connection.
SessionScreen.title: SessionScreen

StagedListing.description: The provisional events a session is holding, for a caller that asked for them.
StagedListing.title: StagedListing

StagingState.description: What a close of this session would consume now, and its fingerprint.
StagingState.title: StagingState

SubmissionReport.description:
Which answer -- a recording, or a written answer -- answers which served task, and
where its judgement stands.

Never the learner's words. A written answer's text is handed to the judge by `pending`
and `claim` and to nobody else; this report reaches the screen, and the read model does
not carry what a learner wrote. The digest says which answer it is without saying what
it says.
SubmissionReport.title: SubmissionReport

TaskAudio.description:
The recording a listening task plays, and how often it may be played.

The allowance sits *inside* this record rather than beside it, so "a replay
allowance where nothing is played" is unrepresentable instead of being a rule
somebody has to write and somebody else has to check.
TaskAudio.title: TaskAudio

TaskPresentation.description:
How one task is rendered. Absent means *free text*, which is not the same thing
as `kind: free-text` with nothing else: an absent record is a pack that has not been
authored for the client, and an explicit one is a decision somebody made.
TaskPresentation.title: TaskPresentation

TrackListEntry.description:
One track as a picker shows it: whose it is and what it is, never how it is set up.

The preferences are left out on purpose. They hold consent decisions and goals, and a
page choosing which track to draw needs a name, not a profile.
TrackListEntry.title: TrackListEntry

VoidedVerdict.description:
A verdict that will never be applied, and why -- by the code a skill acts on and
in the words a learner is shown.
VoidedVerdict.title: VoidedVerdict

WithdrawnSubmission.description:
A submission a command withdrew, and why -- with the held verdicts it voided.

Defined here rather than in `judging`, which imports this module: a run report names
the submissions a transition withdrew, and a model a field is typed with has to exist
when the field does.
WithdrawnSubmission.title: WithdrawnSubmission

WrittenSubmissionReport.description: What became of one written answer. Never its text: the caller sent it.
WrittenSubmissionReport.title: WrittenSubmissionReport

launchToken.description: Minted per server start, handed to the page through the URL fragment, and never written to disk.
launchToken.name: X-LinguaWiki-Token

info.description: Generated from the Pydantic contracts and the server's own route table; never edited by hand. This document describes **shapes, not sequences**. At most one outstanding task per dimension, idempotent serving, scoring against the serve-time snapshot rather than the live pack, and every consent rule live in the service layer and its tests. Conformance to this document is not correctness.\n\nEvery request carries the launch token this server minted when it started; a launchToken is valid for one server start and is never stored.
